content.title: Malaysia: Johor Bahru - The End of Peninsula Malaysia | JB | Overlooking Singapore
content.text: #malaysia #travel #tourism ☕ Please help support my channel by buying me a coffee here: https://www.buymeacoffee.com/willetts... Thank you! 🙏 Located right at the southernmost end of peninsula Malaysia, Johor Bahru (more commonly known as JB) overlooks the island of Singapore. It's a big city – the 2nd largest in Malaysia and and features many activities such as theme parks, golf courses and shopping malls that entice many Singaporeans to visit. In this video, I wander around the very heart of the city which features Chinese shophouses, temples and a small Indian district. I also visit the beautiful Sultan Abu Bakar Mosque, JB's main station as well as a Hindu glass temple. History: Back at the beginning of the 19th century, Johor Bahru was just a small Malay fishing village known as Tanjung Puteri (later Iskander Puteri) and was surrounded by undeveloped jungle. Chinese and Javanese were brought in to clear the land and to develop an agricultural economy. The Chinese planted the area with black pepper and gambier – a shrub that can be used as a tanning agent, dye and food additive, while the Javanese dug canals to drain water from the land, built roads and planted coconuts. The village was renamed Johor Bahru by Sultan Abu Bakar and grew rapidly due to stable government policies, an influx of Chinese immigrants, the construction of the railway and, most importantly, its close proximity to Singapore to which it was linked by the Causeway in 1924. The continuous development of Johor Bahru was, however, halted when the Japanese invaded on the 31st January 1942. The British and other Allied forces were forced to retreat to Singapore and blew up the causeway as a final attempt to stop the Japanese advance in British Malaya. However, in less than a month, the Japanese had repaired the causeway and invaded the Singapore island. After the formation of the Federation of Malaysia in 1963, more development was carried out, with the town's expansion and the construction of more new townships and industrial estates. By the early 1990s, the town had considerably expanded in size, and was officially granted city status on the 1st January 1994.
